items.item_text: 01. Which statement below best describes the highest level of education you have completed? Options: Some High School | High school graduate, diploma or the equivalent (GED) | Some college (less than 60 units) | Associate degree or at least 60 semester units | Bachelor's degree | Master's degree | Professional degree | Doctorate degree

02. How many years of paid or unpaid experience do you have providing community services, family support, or student services to children and families? Options: No experience | Less than 1 year of experience | 1 year but less than 2 years of experience | 2 years but less than 3 years experience | 3 or more years of experience

03. In which setting did you gain most of your experience supporting children and families? Options: K–12 school or school district | Community or social service agency | Government or public agency | Nonprofit organization | Child care or youth program | Other related setting | No related experience

04. Which option best describes your experience working directly with students and families? Options: No experience | I have limited experience assisting students or families. | I have regularly provided information or basic assistance to students and families. | I have regularly assessed student or family needs and provided individualized assistance, referrals, or follow-up services. | I have extensive experience independently supporting students and families with multiple or complex needs, coordinating services, and monitoring outcomes.

05. Based on your community services, family support, or student services experience, please provide details for your MOST RELEVANT positions. For each position, include: (a) Job Title: (b) Organization/Agency Name: (c) Key Relevant Duties: (d) Employment Period: (From MM/YYYY to MM/YYYY) If you have no relevant experience in this area, enter "N/A."

06. Describe a specific time when you identified a need or barrier affecting a student or family and helped connect them with appropriate support or resources. What actions did you take, how did you follow up, and what was the outcome?
07. This position may require bilingual proficiency in Spanish. Are you able to speak, read, and write in Spanish? Options: Yes | No
Serves as liaison between the assigned school site and families of enrolled students, relaying information regarding school standards, requirements, policies, procedures, and District programs.
Conducts outreach to families in support of site attendance, registration, and enrollment activities, including contact regarding chronic absenteeism and non-enrollment.
Communicates with families by telephone, written correspondence, and home visits, concerning student attendance, behavior, academic requirements and progress.
Identifies school and community resources appropriate to student and family needs; refers families to social service agencies, community organizations, and public offices.
Provides ongoing case management for referred students and families, including follow-up on established plans and coordination with social service agencies.
Promotes family participation in school activities, parent education classes, and advisory councils
Interprets and translates for families and staff as assigned.
Updates and maintains contact records, referral documentation, databases, forms, and related data; compiles and prepares reports as needed to support program and administrative activities.
Prepares and distributes correspondence, certificates, notices, and informational materials to families.

Participates in School Attendance Review Board (SARB), Student Attendance Review Team (SART), Student Study Team (SST), and other site and District meetings; attends workshops, trainings, and conferences as assigned.
May operate a vehicle to travel to school sites, community events, and family homes.
Conducts home visits and travels to school sites, family homes, and community locations to meet with students and families.
Performs related duties as assigned.
Community resources, social service agencies, and public offices serving students and families
School objectives, programs, and requirements
Operation of office equipment and recordkeeping techniques
Oral and written communication skills
Interpersonal skills using tact, patience, and courtesy
Values, needs, and concerns of culturally diverse students and families
Interviewing techniques for gathering information
Applicable federal and state laws, codes, and regulations governing pupil attendance, enrollment, and student records
Provide families and District staff with information and referral assistance regarding student attendance, behavior, academic progress, and available health services.
Recognize when students or families would benefit from referral to school or community resources.
Operate a computer and standard office equipment.
Maintain detailed and accurate records and prepare reports.
Communicate both orally and in writing.
Maintain confidentiality and work with discretion.
Establish and maintain effective working relationships with community partners, students, parents, and District staff.
Explain District policies and school program procedures to students, parents, and District staff.
Maintain current knowledge of program rules, regulations, requirements, and restrictions.
Model communications and interactions that respect and include individuals of all languages, abilities, religions, and cultures.
